_comment: Rules for scripts/phone_evidence.py (5.8). Each names a roadmap row (its title and URL) and the events in verification_events.jsonl that close it. A rule is written from the row's closing condition; where the condition also needs a judgement (how something looks), `needs` says so and the rule only proves the mechanism ran. Event names and fields are VerificationJournal.record calls in the app. Conditions may compare with >=N, <=N or !=X, may name the line's own os and ms, and a rule's `absent` lists events that must not appear (phone_evidence.py's docstring).

rules.row: Interactive Deep Think Live Activities (Stop keeps the written text)
rules.needs: During a Deep Think answer, lock the phone and tap Stop on the Lock Screen or Dynamic Island once some text is written.

rules.row: Deep Think and Maximum show progress on the Lock Screen
rules.needs: Ask a Deep Think question and lock the phone until it finishes; glance at the Lock Screen for the step.

rules.row: Long answer outlives 30 s background grant
rules.needs: Ask a Deep Think question, leave the app at once, come back after it would have finished.

rules.row: Question-answering background task had the import's fixed name
rules.needs: Same as the long-answer check.

rules.row: iOS never started the import's background task
rules.needs: Start an import of a large PDF and leave the app for over a minute.

rules.row: iOS ended a background import during overview/tags calls
rules.needs: Import a new file (from Files or Open in), leave the app until the import finishes, then come back to the app. The document ids in import.enrichmentDeferred and import.deferredEnrichment should match.

rules.row: Library built from all-zero vectors when embedding fails
rules.needs: Start an import and leave the app at once.

rules.row: Multi-file imports wait on each file's overview before the next file (5.8)
rules.needs: Add three or more files at once with the app open.

rules.row: Import cards stay on the Lock Screen and Watch after the app is opened (5.8)
rules.needs: Import something, leave the app until it ends, open the app again. Also look at the Watch: the card should be gone.

rules.row: App Store ratings: Apple's sheet only, asked once per version (5.8)
rules.needs: Ask a question in a library with your own documents; Apple's sheet should appear about 2 s after a Verified answer (look for it).

rules.needs: In Safari, share a page to OpenIntelligence, then open the app and accept the import review.

rules.row: Visual Intelligence returns matching documents

rules.row: A Focus filter chooses which libraries show
rules.needs: Add OpenIntelligence's filter to a Focus, pick a library, turn the Focus on and off.

rules.needs: Run Open Library and Open Document from Siri and from Shortcuts on the iPhone, and again on the Mac (check the Mac's journal with --dir).

rules.needs: Say "Open <document name> in OpenIntelligence".

rules.row: Web links open the app, or the App Store

rules.row: Newer transcriber never compiled; recordings use older recognizer
rules.needs: Import a voice memo.

rules.row: Recording language read from two letters in file name

rules.row: App records hangs, slow launches, terminations (MetricKit)

rules.row: Per-state metrics show what gets killed for memory
rules.needs: Nothing: needs a day of use and a termination iOS reports.

rules.row: A local crash report the person can send
rules.needs: Only after a real crash: the next launch offers the report.

rules.row: Deep Think and imports ease off when resources are short
rules.needs: Use the app in Low Power Mode or while the phone is hot; iOS decides when it asks.

rules.row: On PCC, Deep Think/Maximum steps went without evidence
rules.needs: In Deep Think, allow Private Cloud Compute for a long question (iPhone or Mac).

rules.row: "Just Once" PCC consent carries to the next question
rules.needs: In Deep Think choose Just Once, then ask a second Deep Think question that needs Private Cloud Compute (iPhone or Mac).

Then with Always Allow, and again with Don't Allow, run it from the background; once, leave the sheet unanswered with the app unable to show it.

rules.row: Watched folders (5.8)
rules.needs: Library Settings, Watch a Folder, add a file to it, reopen the app.

rules.row: Deep Think and large imports from a shortcut past 30 s
rules.needs: Needs the owner to name RAGAppIntents.swift (patch: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gunnarhostetler-Documents-GitHub-OpenIntelligence/a4f11230-c8a9-44ed-bfbb-f6f8c450ff0f/scratchpad/ragappintents_telemetry.patch). Run an Ask My Documents shortcut set to Deep Think with the app closed; it should finish, with its progress on the Lock Screen (check by eye).

rules.needs: Ask Siri a question about your library, then tap a document, Ask a Follow-Up and Think Deeper on the card (three questions).

rules.row: A library with no vectors cannot repair itself, and the repair reports success
rules.needs: Headless: a Simulator run that stages a library with documents, an empty store and a .paused queue item, then lets self-healing run (pull with --dir from the Simulator's Documents folder).

rules.row: A save that was cut off deleted a library's whole vector index
rules.needs: Import a large PDF (it imports in pieces), force-quit the app from the app switcher mid-import, reopen, and ask a question in that library. The trace line is the proof of the trim; a vectorStore.load event would need the owner to name BNNSVectorDatabase.swift.

rules.row: Spotlight entries are app items that open the right document and re-index on request
rules.needs: On the iPhone, search Spotlight for a document's name and tap the document result (not a passage). Then delete a different document on the Mac and open the iPhone app.
trace: \[Spotlight\] Removed the entries of [1-9]\d* document\(s\) no longer in the libraries

rules.row: Deleting a library races its own background writers, which resurrect it
rules.needs: Mac: open two windows, delete a library in one, quit the app, reopen it (check the Mac's Documents folder with --dir).

rules.row: iCloud sync decoded a library's whole vector store after every piece of an import, and could write it back without the import
rules.needs: On the iPhone, add a file to a library that already has documents, let it finish, swipe the app away, reopen it and ask a question about the new file in that library. The skip is read from its Log.debug line (verbose trace level); a sync.vectorStoreSkipped event would need the owner to name WorkspaceSyncService.swift.
trace: Vector store for \S+ left alone this pass: an import into it has not finished

rules.row: One progress source for import, the Live Activity and long actions
rules.needs: Needs the owner to name RAGAppIntents.swift (patch: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gunnarhostetler-Documents-GitHub-OpenIntelligence/a4f11230-c8a9-44ed-bfbb-f6f8c450ff0f/scratchpad/ragappintents_telemetry.patch). Add several files at once, then while they import say "Check import status in OpenIntelligence" (or run the shortcut) twice.

rules.row: Six file families sync to iCloud without NSFileCoordinator, which generated 599 conflict copies and destroyed data
rules.needs: PARTIAL: proves ten or more sync passes ran and none found a conflict copy (the count is logged only when above 0). Edit the same conversation on the Mac and the iPhone in between. That the other device's edit arrived needs sync.fileFromICloud, which lives in WorkspaceSyncService.swift (hard boundary, needs the owner to name it).
absent_trace: The iCloud folder holds [1-9]\d* conflict copies of library files

rules.row: A rebuild on one device made the other wipe and rebuild the same library, and could delete a document's file
rules.needs: With both devices on 5.8, tap Rebuild on an iCloud library on the iPhone and let it finish, then open the Mac app for a few minutes. This rule reads the iPhone. A twin rule against the Mac's --dir pull uses sync.orphanWipe and rebuild.selfHeal absent.
absent_trace: Wiping orphaned vector database chunks for document

rules.row: Device checks are read off the phone from a development-build event log, not reported by hand
rules.needs: Nothing beyond a day of use with the Debug build; then run python3 scripts/phone_evidence.py.

rules.row: Apple Notes Integration (NotebookLM Style)
rules.needs: Once, in Shortcuts on the iPhone: Find Notes (or a note from the share sheet) into Add to Library's Text, run it, then open the app until the import finishes.

rules.row: Import still runs whole-document passes on the main thread after text cleanup and chunking were moved off it
rules.needs: Import a multi-megabyte Word, PowerPoint or PDF (under 10 MB, so it is not streamed) on the iPhone with the app in front.

rules.row: Paste text, a link or a file into a library
rules.needs: On the iPhone, and again on the Mac (check the Mac app's journal with --dir), copy a file, then a web address, then a paragraph, and tap Paste on the Documents screen after each.

rules.row: "Add Document" and "Ingest Document from Camera" in Shortcuts only open the app
rules.needs: In Shortcuts on the iPhone, run Add a Document, then run Scan a Document.

rules.row: The Atlas reads every passage on the main thread, and on a very large library iOS ends the app
rules.needs: Open the large library (over 60,000 passages), open Visualizations, press Home within a few seconds, come back after a minute.

rules.row: The Atlas named three clusters "API Reference", changed its names between launches, and labelled its axes with stray words
rules.needs: Open the Atlas on your own library, close the app from the app switcher, reopen and open the Atlas again; then say whether the names make sense.

rules.row: Turn on Apple's enhanced security for file parsing
rules.needs: Import a PDF over 10 MB on the iPhone (build with the keys); the memory comparison needs the same import on a build without them, read from the two journals by hand.

rules.row: The app's guides take three of a free plan's five documents
rules.needs: Fresh install on a free plan, tap See It in Action, then add your own documents one at a time up to five.

rules.row: A saved conversation keeps an answer's first 12 passages, so after a relaunch a label past [S12] opens nothing
rules.needs: Ask a question whose answer cites [S13] or later (Standard on a large library), quit the app, open it again, tap that label in the saved answer, then Copy the answer. iPhone or Mac.

rules.row: Adaptive profiles cannot reach Deep Think or Maximum, which is where they would matter most
rules.needs: Turn on adaptive profiles once in the model settings (Mac or iPhone), then ask a Deep Think question that compares two things.
trace: \[Agentic\] Step temperature [0-9.]+ from the adaptive profile

rules.row: Deep Think and Maximum advertised highest-effort reasoning and asked Apple for none on 24 of 25 call sites
rules.needs: On iPhone or Mac, ask one Standard and one Deep Think question that go to Private Cloud Compute (approve the consent sheet, or have Always Allow on). Compare the two events' `reasoning` by eye: the checker does not compare across events.

rules.row: Prompt budgets are counted in characters at a worst-case ratio, so Deep Think and Maximum sessions use a fraction of the on-device window, and a larger window turns structured answers off
rules.needs: Ask a Deep Think question on the Mac (8,192 window) and on the iPhone, with Private Cloud Compute not picked in the model picker. Run the check once per device and read `window` (8192 on the Mac, 4096 on the iPhone if that is its window). Whether the answer came from the right passage is the owner's judgement. The structured-answer limit (the third clause) is not built, so a PASS covers the token plan only.

rules.row: Without Apple Intelligence, a question about the sample documents comes back as stitched excerpts marked Partially Verified
rules.needs: Stock iOS 27 Simulator Debug build (model off) with the samples imported; ask the four suggested sample questions. The journal is read from the simulator's app container, not with devicectl.

rules.row: Question translation uses the high-fidelity strategy where the device supports it
rules.needs: On the iPhone, in a library with a translation language set, ask a question in a different language. Records the session's requested strategy only (TranslationSession.preferredStrategy, the preference it was made with), not what the system used.

rules.row: Nothing said when an answer finished on another tab, and the elapsed clock froze on return
rules.needs: On the iPhone, ask a Deep Think question, open Documents before it finishes, come back to Chat once while it is still running and once after it finished. The expiry part needs an answer that iOS stops in the background, which is rare; the haptic is felt, not logged.

rules.row: The sample library shows "What is nothing?": its curated questions are dead behind a filename match, and the template fallback fails open
rules.needs: On the iPhone, open Chat in the General library while it holds only the sample documents and has no messages.

rules.row: A Pro subscription left permanent Lifetime access behind; from 5.5 only a Lifetime purchase earns it
rules.needs: On a development build with a sandbox account: buy Pro Monthly, wait for it to lapse, open the app again. On an install that had the protection, open the app once.

rules.row: Answers and documents can be handed to other apps as text, Markdown or PDF
rules.needs: Run a shortcut that asks OpenIntelligence a question and passes the answer to Notes or Mail, on the iPhone (or the Mac).

rules.row: Documents and libraries carry real properties in Shortcuts, so the Use Model action and Find get more than a title
rules.needs: On the iPhone, run a shortcut with Find Documents filtered by a property (Library or Type) that passes a document to Use Model, then read the transcript.

rules.row: A menu bar item with a quick ask box on the Mac
rules.needs: Mac: ask a question from the menu bar item's field (Debug build), then check with phone_evidence.py --dir on the Mac container's Documents.

rules.row: Every screen shows you around: a guided tour of tips, one arrow at a time
rules.needs: Settings › How This Works › Show Me Around, then use the app normally: visit Chat, a cited passage, Documents, an import, Library Settings, Atlas, Database, Settings and Plans, and use a control a tip points at.

rules.row: Share an answer as an image card
rules.needs: On the iPhone, tap Image under an answer that has sources and send it in Messages; readability is a glance at the sent card.

rules.needs: Set the iPhone to the largest accessibility text size. In light and then in dark mode, switch to Chat, Documents and Settings and look at each; a judgement only the owner gives.

rules.row: VoiceOver Full Audit
rules.needs: Turn VoiceOver on, ask a question and add a document. Whether VoiceOver reads each screen well (and skips the X-Ray) is still the owner's judgement; the rule proves the flows ran with VoiceOver on.

rules.row: Batch & Drag-and-Drop Document Import
rules.needs: In the Mac app, drop a folder that has a subfolder onto a library.

rules.row: Implement View Entity Annotations (Contextual Screen Awareness)
rules.needs: Open a document's page, then ask Siri about what is on screen.

rules.needs: In the Mac app, import a PDF with a scanned table.

rules.row: Detected entities come from table cells only, so most documents contribute none
rules.needs: Import a PDF (a letter, an invoice) whose body text has a street address.

rules.row: A library asks for its search index to be rebuilt right after an import, and asks again after the rebuild
rules.needs: Import a file into an existing library and ask a question; separately, Rebuild an old library and relaunch.

rules.row: Figures and photos are captioned at import so they can be found
rules.needs: Import a PDF with a chart and ask about a value in it. Whether the answer gives the right value is the owner's look. Whether the answer used the figure's description is read by eye: no field marks a figure passage yet.

rules.row: OpenIntelligence appears under Open in for PDFs and other documents
rules.needs: Drop a PDF on the app's Dock icon on the Mac.

rules.row: A Services menu entry on the Mac: ask about or add the selected text

rules.row: Copy on an answer does nothing on the Mac and still shows the tick
rules.needs: In the Mac app, tap Copy on an answer.

rules.row: Shared links show a title, icon and summary
rules.needs: Share an answer, then Settings > Share the App.

rules.row: Files opened from outside show in a read-only viewer with Add to Library
rules.needs: On the Mac open a PDF with OpenIntelligence, click it in the sheet, then Add to Library.

rules.needs: Nothing to do: it waits for the model to fail this way in real use.

rules.needs: Delete the app from the iPhone and install the build again; import something after a minute.

rules.row: On iPhone the Core AI embedder ran on the GPU at 88 passages a second against 116 to 121 for the Core ML copy; new iPhone and iPad libraries now use Core ML
rules.needs: Import a large PDF on the iPhone, stay in front a minute, then leave the app until it ends.

rules.needs: In the Mac app open Settings > Device & Performance and the Glossary's Context window entry.

rules.row: On a 4,096-token device graph packing gathered 6,000 tokens, so half of each pack was cut by document position
rules.needs: Ask a compare question ("compare A and B") on the iPhone.

rules.row: A citation shows its passage in the document for every kind of file, and says whether it was found
rules.needs: On the iPhone, tap a citation from a PDF, a Word file, a spreadsheet and a recording.

rules.row: The Mac app freezes at launch while iCloud holds a sync file: the sync reads it on the main thread
rules.needs: Nothing: it needs a Mac launch while iCloud is still holding a sync file (after another device wrote). The wait's length is the line's own ms; responsiveness is no main-thread stall before the chat showed (watchdog phase launch). Run with --mac and --since at the launch.

rules.row: Every Mac window runs its own engine and sync, so two windows rebuild and write one library at once
rules.needs: In the Mac app open a second window (File > New Window) and start a Rebuild.

rules.row: Export Results as PDF / Markdown
rules.needs: From the chat menu, Export Conversation as Markdown, JSON Lines and PDF (on the iPhone, then the Mac).
